slides.texte_overlay:
How to negotiate your salary
without being pushy
Never give the first number. When they ask what you expect, say "What's the range for this role?" Whoever names a number first usually sets the ceiling, and it's rarely in your favour.
Thank them for the offer, then ask for time. "Thanks, I'm excited about this. Can I come back to you by Thursday?" Nobody serious says yes to a big decision on the spot.
Negotiate the whole package. Salary, start date, remote days, training budget, holidays. If they can't move on money, they can often move on something else that matters to you.
Use their words. "You mentioned you need someone who can lead the project from day one. That's exactly why I'm asking for this level." Linking your ask to their need makes it easy to accept.
Before: nervous, accepting the first number. After: five minutes a day of history, art or science, and a calmer, sharper head in every tough conversation, including this one.

slides.texte_overlay: Stay warm the whole time. You're about to work with these people. Friendly, clear and patient gets better offers than aggressive and demanding, every single time.
Get the final offer in writing before you resign anywhere. Verbal promises change. A written offer with the number, the date and the title protects you, and it's completely normal to ask.
